<신1:1~5> 이 율법 설명하기를 시작하였더라: <Deut 1:1~5> began Moses to declare this law
신명기는 율법 설명서, 되풀이 할 신, 명령 명: Deuteronomy is an explanation of the law. In Korean it's "Sinmyeonggi": "sin" means to repeat, "myeong" means command
한 마디로 모세의 고별 설교: In a word, Moses's farewell sermon
가나안 입성을 앞둔 이스라엘 백성. 대체로 젊은 세대를 보고 간곡히 부탁: The people of Israel, about to enter Canaan. He pleads earnestly, looking mostly at the young generation. The generation that had personally experienced the tremendous events of the Exodus had all died, and now, looking at the young generation, he felt the need to explain the contents of the covenant once more. I'm doing this with Moses's heart too...
The content mostly overlaps with Leviticus. The order is free.
5장에 보면 언약의 대상을 다시 명확히 이 언약은, 이 율법은 죽은 너희: In chapter 5 he makes clear again who the covenant is with: this covenant, this law, wasn't made only with your fathers who have died. It isn't something you can keep halfway or not keep at all. He made it with us, who are alive here today.
29장 14절에는 이렇게 말해요. 내가 이 언약과 맹세를 너희에게만 세: In chapter 29 verse 14 he says this: Neither with you only do I make this covenant and this oath; but with him that standeth here with us this day before the LORD our God, and also with him that is not here with us this day:
미래 세대들도 해당 된다고 말하고 있죠? 그러니까 이 언약은, 이 율법은: He's saying it applies to future generations too, right? So this covenant, this law, is an everlasting statute that every generation to come must keep. What about us? We didn't hear it directly, but we heard it indirectly, didn't we?
우리도 율법의 정신을 가지고 살아야 합니다. 왜냐하면 율법은 너무 기본기: We too must live with the spirit of the law. Because the law is just the basics. It's silly to emphasize the law. It's kindergarten level.
그래서 예수님께서 다 업그레이드 하시잖아요. 옛 사람에게는 너희가 이렇게: That's why Jesus upgrades it all, right? Ye have heard that it was said by them of old time... but I say unto you.... love your enemies. Like that.
1) 지금도 이스라엘 사람들은 말씀 그대로 실천하기 위해 이런 걸 쓴다: 1) Even today, Israelis use things like these to put the word into practice literally
경문갑 – 미간에 붙여 표로 삼고: Phylactery box – bound between the eyes as frontlets
테필린 – 손목에 매서 기호를 삼은: Tefillin – bound on the wrist as a sign
메추자 – 집 문설주와 바깥 문에 오며 가며 만지고 키스: Mezuzah – on the doorposts of the house and on the gates; they touch and kiss it coming and going
Our house's front door
 2) The only verse in the Bible that says to write it and put it up.
<신5:6~21> 나는 너를 애굽 땅에서 종 되었던 집에서 인도하여 낸:
<Deut 5:6~21> I am the LORD thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt from the house of bondage.
 ① Thou shalt have none other gods before me.
 ② Thou shalt not make thee any graven image
 ③ Thou shalt not take the name of the LORD thy God in vain
1 모세가 십계명의 1~3계명을 해석한 것이 쉐마다. 가만히 들여다 보니: 1 The Shema is Moses's interpretation of commandments 1~3 of the Ten Commandments. Look at it closely and it's just like what a girlfriend says. Suppose she said, ‘Babe~ from now on, look only at me~ don't even think about other girls~ don't talk carelessly about me in front of other people~’. What does that mean? It means love only me, right?
사랑해 달라는 말은 억수로 사랑한다는 말입니다.\n 2) 4계명, 안식일:
Saying "love me" means "I love you like crazy."
 2) The 4th commandment, the Sabbath commandment, is not a commandment for God but a commandment for people.
레위기 할 때 설명 했었죠? 그러므로 1~3계명까지가 하나님을 위한 계:
I explained this when we did Leviticus, right? So commandments 1~3 are commandments for God, and commandments 4~10 are commandments for people
 3) The 5th commandment: Honour thy father and thy mother ("honor", not "harass") that thy days may be prolonged in the land - there's a promise of long life. When you honor the ones who brought you into being, that shows your existence has worth. But if you honor God, our eternal Father, you don't just live long, you get eternal life.
 4) The 6th commandment: Thou shalt not murder
 - It's mistranslated. The original says, thou shalt not kill. It's not just that you mustn't kill people; you mustn't kill anything that has life.
 5) The 7th commandment: Thou shalt not commit adultery
 6) The 8th commandment: Thou shalt not steal
 7) The 9th commandment: Thou shalt not bear false witness
법정 용어로 거짓 증거 하지 말라. 벌 받을 놈이 상받고 상받을 사람이:
"Don't bear false witness" is a legal term. If someone who deserves punishment gets rewarded and someone who deserves reward gets punished, you know what breaks? Justice breaks. When justice breaks, nobody does good.
 8) The 10th commandment: Thou shalt not covet.
 - The hardest commandment of the ten. Covetousness is idolatry. If we don't let go of the thought of getting something, that thought ends up leading our lives. Wanting it so badly, you end up doing anything at all.
광야 생활의 목적: The purpose of the wilderness life
<신8:2~3> 네 하나님 여호와께서 이 사십 년 동안에 너로 광야의 길:
<Deut 8:2~3> And thou shalt remember all the way which the LORD thy God led thee these forty years in the wilderness, to humble thee, and to prove thee, to know what was in thine heart, whether thou wouldest keep his commandments, or no. And he humbled thee, and suffered thee to hunger, and fed thee with manna, which thou knewest not, neither did thy fathers know; that he might make thee know that man doth not live by bread only, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of the LORD doth man live.
 ① To humble us - you have to be humbled to receive grace
 ② To find out whether we keep His commandments or not - He surely tests whether we obey God's word
 ③ To show that if you listen well to God, making a living is no problem
13장 기적과 꿈꾸는 자 조심하라\n 1) 이적과 기적이 일어나도 쉬이:
Chapter 13: Beware of miracles and dreamers
 1) He says even if signs and wonders happen, don't be easily shaken and don't follow, right? And He says the dreamer is to be put to death. There are 3 times in the Bible when lots of miracles show up: first at the Exodus, then when the prophets appear, and then when Jesus came. What's in common? When God needed to reveal Himself. We shouldn't keep asking Him to show us miracles.
이 말씀은 아직 이스라엘의 왕이 생기기도 전에 하신 말씀- 전지하신 하나: This word was spoken before Israel even had a king - the all-knowing God
He must be set up only from among their own people, there are 3 things he must not do, and one thing he must do.
20장에 보면 이스라엘의 3대 희락 5~9절\n 1) 하나님은 여유로우:
If you look at chapter 20, Israel's 3 great joys, verses 5~9
 1) God is a cool, easygoing God
 - Israel's 3 great joys
① The joy of planting a fruit tree and picking the first fruit: you can eat it after 5 years
② The joy of building a house and holding its dedication
③ The joy of getting engaged to a maiden and holding the wedding
이 기쁨을 즐기지 못한 사람은 전쟁이 나도 돌려보내라 하신다. 얼마나 멋: He says anyone who hasn't enjoyed these joys should be sent home, even when war breaks out. What a cool God He is.
강좌 시작할 때 봤었죠? 가나안 땅에 들어가면 7년에 한 번이라도 율법을: We saw it when we started the course, right? When you enter the land of Canaan, read the law to the people at least once every 7 years. But Joshua doesn't do it.
도데체 왜 안했는지 모르겠어요. 여호수아가 안 하니 그 후의 사람들도 다: I really don't know why he didn't. Since Joshua didn't, everyone after him didn't either. So the history of the Old Testament is all a history of disobedience, a history of getting beaten. And then, almost 800 years later, in Ezra's time, this command is kept for the first time. At that time the people weep and wail and it's a huge commotion.
31장 16절 한 번 보세요. 하나님께서는 이미 이스라엘 백성들이 배신: Take a look at chapter 31 verse 16. God already knows the people of Israel will betray Him. Folks, have you ever been betrayed? I have. It's bad enough when you don't see it coming, but being betrayed when you know it's coming drives you crazy. But God, even knowing everything, still has hopes. I really couldn't understand this. Why hope when you know full well it won't work out? When you know they won't do it...
제가 자식을 낳아 보니까 알겠더라고요. 잔소리를 자꾸하게 되요. 근데 당: When I had kids, I understood. You keep nagging. But I know it won't get fixed right away. And even knowing it won't work, you still hope. Why? Because you love them.
사랑하지 않으면 관심 자체도 없는 겁니다. 사랑하니까 잔소리라도 하는 겁: If you don't love someone, you don't even care. Because you love them, you at least nag. Because you love them, you hope. And when that hope is shattered, you get angry too. Folks, when you lose something precious, you turn your desk upside down, right? You open every drawer.... and then what? You open the drawer you already opened, right? Then you look somewhere else and open that drawer again, right? You already checked it wasn't there. So why open it again? Because what you're looking for is so precious...
여러분이 하나님께 그렇게 소중한 존재예요. 그러니까 여기 오게 해서 이런: You are that precious to God. That's why He has you come here and hear this word. Even knowing you won't listen... haha
